docs.purpose: A grid of who is allowed to see and change what — every role down one axis, every table and route across the other. It is built by asking the live database what its access rules actually are and re-running the app's own route classifier, rather than by reading what a migration file claims. That distinction is the whole point: this page shows the permissions that are really in force, and flags any place where the declared intent and the live database disagree.

checks.why: Spec 126 §6.2 rule 3: it FAILS on a table with RLS enabled and no declared class, a policy live but not in the seed, and a seed row with no live policy. Bidirectional, and it gates the render because a half-true access matrix is worse than none.

The fourth failure condition of the same rule: surface.guards.session must equal contract.guards.auth_class. The measured defect is /builders gated authenticated while /api/builders is public via PUBLIC_PREFIXES:71 — the page is behind a login, the data it renders is not.
Spec 126 §6.2 rule 2: every role in the closed set appears on every row, including the ones whose answer is "none" with a why_none — an unwritten "none" is most dangerous exactly here.

R-11: migration 226's own comment records that prevent_is_admin_self_escalation is bypassable by the table owner. The page must render D5 as a declared OPEN row; a matrix that renders a guarantee the DB does not enforce is worse than no matrix.
If the catalog read fails the page must say so; an empty grid would read as "no policies exist", which is the most dangerous possible false negative on this page.
A grant/deny grid conveyed by cell colour alone is unreadable without labels.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND policyname !~ '^[a-z0-9_]+_(select|insert|update|delete)_(own|own_admin|admin)$'
invariants.why: Spec 114 §8 fixes the name as <table>_<operation>_<scope>; a policy outside that shape cannot be joined to a seed row, so it would render as an orphan of the matrix rather than as itself.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relrowsecurity AND c.relname NOT IN (SELECT tablename FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname='public')
invariants.why: This count is Class B by construction — RLS enabled with zero policies IS the deny-all posture — so it is descriptive, not a threshold; naming it stops a reviewer reading a large number as a gap.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname = 'public'
plausibility.why: Measured today: 26 CREATE POLICY statements (2 in migration 226, 24 in 230, 0 in 231). A live count far below that means policies were dropped; far above means someone created them outside the reviewed-migration path, which Spec 126 §6.2 rule 4 exists to prevent.

plausibility.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='public' AND c.relrowsecurity
plausibility.why: Measured today: 87 ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY lines, 69 of them migration 227's Class-B default-deny sweep. A drop here is a table that quietly lost its default deny.
